Patch Set 2:

(3 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Looks good; the new check is correct and only fires where the pre-pass would also have refused. A few optional items inline for whenever the patch is next refreshed, no need to re-spin for them. Should 160Ac get a case for the new refusal? One way to make the purge land mid-run on a two-MDT setup: give MDT0000 enough matches to fill a pipe that nobody is reading yet, so `lfs find` blocks during the MDT0000 scan. Then clear MDT0001 past the cookie, drain the pipe, and check for -ESTALE and an unchanged cookie.

commit.subject: LU-20650 lfs: find --since-cookie, check each MDT when read
commit.message:
LU-20650 lfs: find --since-cookie, check each MDT when read

The stale check runs on every MDT before any of them is read, so that
a refusal comes before the first match is printed. But a purge can
reach a later MDT while an earlier one is being read. Then that MDT's
scan starts at the oldest record left, the records between the anchor
and it are gone, and the run ends with rc 0 and a short answer.

So llapi_find_since() reads the oldest record again just before each
later MDT is scanned, through find_cookie_purged(), the purge test
find_cookie_check() now shares: one find_cl_first() record each. If it
is past anchor + 1, the run stops with -ESTALE and names both numbers.
The matches already printed stay printed. The cookie is not rewritten,
so every later run is refused the same way until it is removed, rather
than skip the purged records.

The check reads the log, not the scan's own stream. Under coalescing
the stream gives one record per object, with its latest index, so the
first index it delivers says nothing about what was purged.

Still not covered, and the man pages say so: a purge that empties the
log (seen once new records arrive), a purge on the MDT being read,
which is the only window on a single-MDT filesystem, and a record
written late at the tail of a busy log.
